ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, for square $ABCD$ with a side length of 1, $O$ is the midpoint of diagonal $BD$. Point $M$ is on side $AB$, and $BM=2AM$. Point $N$ is on side $BC$, and $BN=AM$. Lines $AN$ and $MD$ intersect at point $P$. Connect $OP$. What is the length of $OP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let AN and BD intersect at point Q,\\
since the side length of square ABCD is 1,\\
therefore $BD=\sqrt{AB^2+AD^2}=\sqrt{2}$,\\
since $BM=2AM$,\\
therefore $BM+AM=AB=1$,\\
therefore $AM=BN=\frac{1}{3}$, $BM=\frac{2}{3}$,\\
since $AD\parallel BN$,\\
therefore $\triangle NQB\sim \triangle AQD$,\\
therefore $\frac{BN}{AD}=\frac{BQ}{QD}=\frac{NQ}{AQ}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
therefore $DQ=3BQ$,\\
therefore $DQ=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}$, $BQ=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$,\\
since O is the midpoint of BD,\\
therefore $OD=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
therefore $OQ=DQ-OD=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$,\\
In $\triangle ADM$ and $\triangle BAN$,\\
$\begin{cases}AD=AB\\ \angle DAM=\angle ABN\\ AM=BN\end{cases}$,\\
therefore $\triangle ADM\cong \triangle BAN$ (SAS),\\
therefore $\angle ADM=\angle BAN$,\\
since $\angle PAD+\angle BAN=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle PAD+\angle ADM=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle APD=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle DAM=90^\circ$, $AM=\frac{1}{3}$, $AD=1$,\\
therefore $DM= \sqrt{AM^2+AD^2}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}$,\\
since $S_{\triangle ADM}=\frac{1}{2}\times AD\cdot AM=\frac{1}{2}\times DM\cdot AP$,\\
therefore $AP=\frac{1\times \frac{1}{3}}{\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}$,\\
therefore $PM=\sqrt{AM^2-AP^2}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}$,\\
therefore $PD=DM-PM=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}$,\\
since $\triangle ADM\cong \triangle BAN$,\\
therefore $AN=DM= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}$,\\
since $\frac{NQ}{AQ}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
therefore $NQ=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{12}$, $AQ=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{4}$,\\
therefore $PQ=AQ-AP=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{20}$,\\
As shown in the diagram, draw OG$\perp$DM at point G through point O,\\
since $OG\parallel PQ$,\\
therefore $\triangle OGD\sim \triangle QPD$,\\
therefore $\frac{DO}{DQ}=\frac{DG}{DP}=\frac{OG}{QP}=\frac{2}{3}$,\\
therefore $DG=\frac{2}{3}DP=\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}$, $OG=\frac{2}{3}QP=\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{20}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}$,\\
therefore $PG=DP-DG=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}-\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}$,\\
therefore $OP=\sqrt{OG^2+PG^2}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{10}}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

Since $AD\parallel BN$, therefore $\triangle NQB\sim \triangle AQD$, therefore $\frac{BN}{AD}=\frac{BQ}{QD}=\frac{NQ}{AQ}=\frac{1}{3}$. Therefore $DQ=3BQ$, therefore $DQ=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}$, $BQ=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$. Since $O$ is the midpoint of $BD$, therefore $OD=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, therefore $OQ=DQ-OD=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$. In $\triangle ADM$ and $\triangle BAN$, $\begin{cases}AD=AB\\ \angle DAM=\angle ABN\\ AM=BN\end{cases}$, therefore $\triangle ADM\cong \triangle BAN$ (SAS), therefore $\angle ADM=\angle BAN$. Since $\angle PAD+\angle BAN=90^\circ$, therefore $\angle PAD+\angle ADM=90^\circ$, therefore $\angle APD=90^\circ$. Since $\angle DAM=90^\circ$, $AM=\frac{1}{3}$, $AD=1$, therefore $DM=\sqrt{AM^2+AD^2}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}$. Since $S_{\triangle ADM}=\frac{1}{2}\times AD\cdot AM=\frac{1}{2}\times DM\cdot AP$, therefore $AP=\frac{1\times \frac{1}{3}}{\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}$. Therefore $PM=\sqrt{AM^2-AP^2}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}$, therefore $PD=DM-PM=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}$. Since $\triangle ADM\cong \triangle BAN$, therefore $AN=DM=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}$. Since $\frac{NQ}{AQ}=\frac{1}{3}$, therefore $NQ=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{12}$, $AQ=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{4}$. Therefore $PQ=AQ-AP=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{20}$. As shown in the diagram, draw $OG\perp DM$ at point $G$ through point $O$. Since $OG\parallel PQ$, therefore $\triangle OGD\sim \triangle QPD$, therefore $\frac{DO}{DQ}=\frac{DG}{DP}=\frac{OG}{QP}=\frac{2}{3}$. Therefore $PG=DP-DG=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{10}-\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}$, therefore $OP=\sqrt{OG^2+PG^2}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{10}}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

Also BN=AM=1/3, and N is on BC, so N=(1,1/3). O is the midpoint of BD, so O=((1+0)/2,(0+1)/2)=(1/2,1/2).

The line AN passes through (0,0) and (1,1/3), and its equation is y=x/3. The line MD passes through (1/3,0) and (0,1), its slope is -3, and its equation is y=1-3x. The intersection point P satisfies x/3=1-3x, so 10x/3=1, x=3/10, y=1/10, namely P=(3/10,1/10).

Thus OP=sqrt((1/2-3/10)^2+(1/2-1/10)^2)=sqrt((1/5)^2+(2/5)^2)=sqrt(1/25+4/25)=sqrt(1/5)=sqrt(5)/5.
